baer-heitev/21:_: Shovet. And if a heap of stones fell upon it, it is forbidden to move the stones in order to take it. Tur — gemara.
beer-hagolah/1:ד: Tur in the name of the Ramban
beer-hagolah/8:ד: Tur in the name of the Ramban
beer-hagolah/12:_: Beraisa there, and Rav Papa and Rav Matana there, and per one explanation that is the Rosh, and as was explained below at the end of siman 690 — Beit Yosef wrote so.
beer-hagolah/17:_: Tur in the name of the Ramban
beer-hagolah/19:_: Tur in the name of the Ramban
beer-hagolah/22:_: Hagahot Osheri in chapter 2 of Rosh Hashana, and Tur in siman 255 in the name of Rashba and Shulchan Piskei.
beur-hagra/3:ד: Meiri. There (46) 1, and see Tosafos there:
beur-hagra/8:ו: And if they glued, etc. The Rosh there to the Raavad, and all this is not as he [said]. And his reason is because we learn in the mishna: A shofar that cracked, etc., glued, etc. — it implies that the first clause also [refers] only to one cracked entirely, similar to broken shofar pieces.
biur-halacha/3:ב: Rather when it was annulled from erev Yom Tov — see Mishna Berurah what we wrote, that if it was not annulled at the time he sanctified the day, etc. The source of our words is from Rashi's language in Sukkah daf 33a s.v. v'lulav misukah lo yalif, and likewise there, in column 2 s.v. hig, see there. However, in truth it is difficult — for behold the time of the lulav mitzvah begins from dawn onward, and if so even if it was annulled at night it is as before the time. And I found the Baal Aruch LaNer stood on this there, and see there that he elaborated on this. However, also from the language of the Gemara there which says 'if we say from yesterday's morning,' etc. — it also implies like Rashi, and tzarich iyun:
biur-halacha/7:ב: That one should not blow with a pierced shofar — in Beit Yosef he brought this in the name of Kol Bo and the responsum of the Rosh; and in truth this is also found in the Rambam's commentary on the Mishna, and thus: 'And if it was pierced, there are laws about it — namely that one must seal the hole,' etc., and it clearly implies that he interprets the mishna as the second explanation of Kol Bo that was brought in Beit Yosef, see there. And likewise Ritva wrote that the Bavli disagrees with the Yerushalmi on this; and per Bavli, if they did not seal it at all it is invalid if it hinders the tekiah. And here I saw something somewhat surprising in the words of Peri Megadim in our matter — in section 7 in Mishbetzos Zahav he leans that even per Mechaber's view, who is lenient regarding a pierced shofar, nevertheless we require even on a long shofar that at least the majority of the shofar be whole without holes; and if so, according to this the Rama who is strict would forbid blowing with it l'chatchila even in this manner. And in section 9 he leans that even according to Rama's view, if the majority is whole, one could say one may blow with it l'chatchila. And perhaps because the matter is not clear to him he leans here and there; and we already wrote inside that if the sound is clear one should not be strict about it, especially when the majority is whole:
biur-halacha/8:ב: Even if they glued with glue — see Mishna Berurah what we wrote, that cracked is different from pierced, for the glue is not recognizable between the glue layers; and in pierced it deals there that they sealed with another piece [Rosh]. And he wrote there Korban Nesanel: he speaks of the manner of the matter, and the same applies if one sealed the hole with glue; and the main reason is since it is missing it is recognizable, end quote. And see in Peri Megadim who leans somewhat that even in a hole that has a deficiency, if it is small (meaning very small) and one can place glue there — it is as though of its kind, meaning since it is not recognizable:
chatam-sofer/3:_: (there, in Magen Avraham section 5) as stated in Avodah Zarah. NB see responsa Chasam Sofer Orach Chayyim siman 179. Explanation of Rashi's words there — see Machatzit HaShekel who pressed [the point].
eliyah-rabbah/23:_: [23] [Levush] rather he blew on the wide side, etc. So he wrote at the end of siman 590, and also on the Rama requires study — what did he innovate here.
kaf-hachayyim/2:_: 2) There. His mitzvah is with a ram's [horn] and bent. A ram's [horn] so that we remember the binding of Isaac (for which a ram was in his place), and bent so that they bend their hearts in prayer. Tur from the gemara. Magen Avraham section 1. And a ram is from thirteen months and one day and above; but before this time it is not called a ram, as written in chapter 1 of tractate Parah — see there.
kaf-hachayyim/14:_: 14) There. And likewise horns of most animals, etc. — such as of the re'em and deer. Beit Yosef in the name of the Ran. Mishna Berurah Orach Chayyim 7. And if the re'em is a pure species — see Peri Chadash and Mateh Yehuda who wrote that it is a pure wild-animal species, unlike Knesset HaGedolah in Hagahot Beit Yosef who wrote plainly that it is an impure species — see there. And likewise Magen Avraham section 3, and likewise Knesset HaGedolah himself retracted as written in the hints of his responsa to Yoreh De'ah that were printed at the end of Kol Ben Levi siman 179 — see there. And Machatzik HaBracha brought it Orach Chayyim 2.
kaf-hachayyim/17:_: 17) There — gloss. And likewise a shofar from an impure animal is invalid. Because it is said: "so that the Torah of God shall be in your mouth" — everything in the Torah of God must be from what is permitted in your mouth. And even though it is of neveilah or another prohibition, we apply to your mouth [the rule] "from what is permitted in your mouth," as we say regarding tefillin and a Torah scroll; and the same applies to every heavenly craft that is permitted in your mouth. Levush. Taz. Magen Avraham section 3. However, the Ran in the chapter "They saw" of Bava Batra wrote that this which we say in the chapter of Bava Metzia (daf 28): "They were not qualified for heavenly craft except from a pure animal" — and a shofar too is heavenly craft, since it comes for remembrance — is not a complete proof; and therefore the matter requires further study — see there. And Bach, Beit Yosef, and see there Orach Chayyim 1. And therefore the see-there wrote that if there is no other shofar, one should blow with such a [shofar] without a berachah. And likewise Mateh Efraim Orach Chayyim 3, Mishna Berurah Orach Chayyim 8.
kaf-hachayyim/20:_: 20) There. One who steals a shofar and blows with it — he fulfilled [the obligation], etc. However, there is an opinion that a stolen shofar is invalid — and that is such as when one stole an entire shofar from its owner, for that is forbidden; but if he stole a horn and shaped it into a shofar, he owes him money and it is kosher, as explained in Beit Yosef — see there. And Bach, Taz. And nafka mina: if afterward another shofar was designated for him, or he obtained permission from the owner of the shofar he stole from — he should return and blow with it in order to fulfil according to all opinions; but he should not bless, since it is clear that b'dieved one fulfilled with a stolen [shofar], and even though he did not bless at first on a stolen shofar, as written in the section that follows, and see below Orach Chayyim 24.
kaf-hachayyim/21:_: 21) There. One who steals a shofar and blows with it — he fulfilled [the obligation], etc. And nevertheless one does not bless on it. Magen Avraham section 4. Eliyah Rabbah Orach Chayyim 7, Chayei Adam siman 141 seif 2, Razin Orach Chayyim 4, Chayei Adam kelal 140 Orach Chayyim 18, Mateh Efraim Orach Chayyim 4, Mishna Berurah Orach Chayyim 9. And even if he acquired it through despair and change of ownership, one could say he should not bless — Eliyah Rabbah Orach Chayyim 4, and likewise Maharikash, for just as we say below siman 649 regarding a stolen lulav — even if he acquired it through change he should not bless on it — the same applies here. However, Peri Chadash disagrees and wrote that this case is different, for the berachah is only on the hearing, and in hearing theft is not relevant — it is fine to bless on it in every case, see there. And likewise is the view of Mateh Efraim there. But Mateh Yehuda brought the words of Maharikash and the aforementioned Peri Chadash and wrote that the main [view] is not to bless, see there. And likewise Hanhagot siman 2 on the words of the aforementioned Peri Chadash that it is not obligatory, and he concluded: nevertheless for practical halachah it should be only a doubt in berachot — one may be lenient, see there. And likewise Mishna Berurah there that even if there was despair and change of ownership, or change through action, likewise it is not fit to bless. And see above siman 25 Orach Chayyim 86 and below siman 649.
kaf-hachayyim/22:_: 22) However — it is clear that even if one acquired a stolen shofar, he should not blow with it if he has another suitable one, lest it become his advocate his prosecutor, as we say regarding lulav in Yerushalmi derech perek lulav hagazul. Peri Chadash. Mishna Berurah in Shaar HaTziyun 19. And regarding blessing, Peri Chadash's view appears to be to bless, and likewise Mateh Efraim there. But other Acharonim hold one does not bless, as written in the previous Orach Chayyim.
kaf-hachayyim/23:_: 23) And it appears — it is permitted to take a friend's shofar without his knowledge and bless on it, as written siman 649 seif 5. And even though a shofar spoils somewhat through its blowing, behold a talit also spoils somewhat, and nevertheless it is permitted, as written above siman 14. And there is no concern that he will blow in it extensively like with books (above siman 14 Orach Chayyim 31) — for why would he blow more than his obligation? Magen Avraham there. Eliyah Rabbah there. Razin Orach Chayyim 5, Chayei Adam there. And nevertheless one may blow a hundred blasts with it, since they are accustomed to blow in this measure. Mateh Efraim Orach Chayyim 5, Mishna Berurah there. And it implies — however, for learning it is forbidden to take without the owner's knowledge unless he knows his friend is not particular about this. Chayei Adam there. And that which it is permitted to take a friend's shofar, etc. — that is to blow with it in the place where it rests; but to remove it from his house to the synagogue, or the reverse, is forbidden, lest he be particular about it and it is theft, as written above siman 14 seif 4 and in our words there Orach Chayyim 19 and 22 — see there. And likewise Magen Avraham siman 649 section 16 regarding lulav — see there. And likewise Mishna Berurah in this siman in Shaar HaTziyun 20.
machatzit-hashekel/3:ד: And that which the see-there wrote "we do not rule," etc. — his intent is to challenge the Rama who ruled like this [view] of the Ran. For thus said the Ran: Perhaps specifically regarding pure ones (kosher shofarot), but impure ones not. For we say in the chapter "With what may one light" daf 28: Rabbi Yose taught: They were not qualified for heavenly craft except from a pure animal; and a shofar too is heavenly craft, for we say in Rosh Hashana daf 26a — one reason that a cow's horn is invalid for a shofar: an accuser may not become an advocate — not to mention the sin of the calf with the calf. For from this reason [the cow's horn] is not used inside in golden garments — not to mention the sin of the golden calf. And it challenges: but it is used in golden garments outside; and a shofar too is outside. And it answers: a shofar too, since it comes for remembrance to raise the remembrance of Israel to their Father in heaven, is considered as inside (for the Gemara compares shofar blowing to inner service; therefore it requires that it be from a pure animal, for it is heavenly craft). However, it is not a complete proof, etc., end quote. And it is — the Ran was uncertain; Rama ruled strictly to disqualify from an impure animal. And on this the see-there challenged: for the Ran's reason to disqualify is because Rabbi Yose taught "they were not qualified," etc., and we do not rule thus like Rabbi Yose, since a verse was needed for tefillin that they be written on the hide of a pure animal, as written: "so that the Torah of God shall be in your mouth," and we derive "from what is permitted in your mouth." And if we ruled that they were not qualified for heavenly craft — why do I need a verse?
machatzit-hashekel/3:ז: Also it appears to me that the re'em is pure, etc. — he intended to disagree with the see-there who wrote: from that which Tosafos wrote in Rosh Hashana daf 26 s.v. chutz, etc., on this which we learned there: All shofarot are kosher except of a cow. And Tosafos wrote thus: That which it does not also teach "except of a re'em," etc., and perhaps they are not hollow and are not fit for a shofar — so far his words. And the see-there wrote on this: And if the re'em is an impure species, it is proven from their words that other impure [animals] are kosher for a shofar, end quote. (And in truth according to his view it should have been a challenge on the Ran who wrote that a shofar from an impure animal is invalid. And he wrote afterward as Tosafos wrote: from this reason the mishna does not teach "except of a re'em," because it is not fit for a shofar since it is not hollow, see-there. And therefore it must be that the re'em is pure — since he did not say that in any case it is invalid because it is impure, as the see-there inferred from Tosafos. Or one could say: since the Ran himself was not clear that a shofar of an impure animal is invalid, therefore he took the answer that suffices with certainty — because it is not hollow. If so, one could also explain the Tosafos.) And therefore Magen Avraham wrote that it is certainly pure, and there is nothing to infer from Tosafos at all:
machatzit-hashekel/5:א: (section 5) He intended to acquire, etc. — and specifically idolatry of a non-Jew: if a Jew acquired it, it has no annulment. But ornaments or decoration of a non-Jew's idolatry — even if a Jew acquired it, the Rabbenu Yerucham ruled in Yoreh De'ah siman 146 seif 2 that it has annulment. However, Bach there disagrees, as Shach wrote in his name section 1:
machatzit-hashekel/5:ה: And the reason: since a Jew is liable, etc. — in truth the plain meaning of Rashi's language in Avodah Zarah there implies like Bach, who wrote thus s.v. ella, etc.: a decree lest he raise it for her and acquire it for her through raising — for everything ownerless, such as a found object, is acquired through raising, end quote. And since a reason was needed [that] all ownerless [property], etc. — it implies like Bach that it deals specifically with ownerless property. And Magen Avraham must hold that he holds: since Rava did not explain in the explanation of the Gemara in Avodah Zarah "of ownerless," therefore it deals even with [property] that has an owner. Nevertheless, since through raising it becomes idolatry of a Jew, since he is liable for damages. But why is it said that through raising he is liable for damages? Thus Rashi: he acquires it through raising to become liable for accidents — for all ownerless [property] is acquired through raising with a complete acquisition; therefore in any case when it has an owner, it is that he does not acquire a complete acquisition through raising; nevertheless he acquires it for the purpose of liability to become liable for accidents:
machatzit-hashekel/5:ז: So wrote Beit Yosef in Yoreh De'ah in Tur according to some versions in Tur:
machatzit-hashekel/6:א: (section 6) When it was annulled, etc. — if so it is rejected, etc. — these are the words of the Mordekhai, who is among those who are strict, that Rama wrote, that Rama wrote: since in tractate Avodah Zarah daf 47a it was unresolved and not explained whether there is deferral regarding a mitzvah; if we say he returns and it is seen — therefore they go to be strict:
machatzit-hashekel/6:ג: Even if it was seen and rejected, etc. — and in Beit Yosef. Meaning: in Sukkah daf 33 we say: How is it — the grapes blackened from erev Yom Tov? At that time they disqualify, for as long as they are green they do not disqualify; therefore when they blackened from erev Yom Tov, which is deferral from the outset before Yom Tov entered — then the deferral begins. And certainly it returns and is seen. But how is it — they blackened on Yom Tov, which is seen and rejected? For when Yom Tov entered it was kosher, and on Yom Tov when they blackened it was rejected. On this the Gemara was unresolved whether they are diminished or return and are seen. And nevertheless the Rambam ruled that in such a case too it returns and is seen; and likewise ruled the Rosh, see-there siman 646, [and] what Rabbenu Yerucham wrote in settling the matter, even though it was an unresolved matter that was not explained, and see-there also in Taz:
machatzit-hashekel/6:ז: As Tosafos wrote in Avodah Zarah s.v. mi ma'is, etc. — and that is according to Maharsha's explanation there, and not like Maharam Lublin, see-there. And with this are resolved, etc., that always Rava who said "he fulfilled" deals before annulment; and the unresolved matter of Rabbi Levi is after annulment — whether it is permitted l'chatchila or whether there is deferral. And regarding l'chatchila — behold it was rejected before annulment. Or there is no deferral and even l'chatchila it is permitted. And also the rest of the difficulties of Tosafos there were settled:
machatzit-hashekel/6:ח: And if so the law is thus — meaning according to Tur and Beit Yosef; not so according to those who are strict whom Rama brought.
machatzit-hashekel/11:א: (section 11) And a remainder remained, etc. — as Bach wrote explicitly regarding a hole. And from this reason Taz wrote in truth that the Shulchan Aruch deals specifically when its voice was changed through the piercing — its law is like one plated with gold on the outside in seif 16; and see Peri Chadash who also wrote that he did not know the reason for this law:
machatzit-hashekel/20:_: (section 20) A hole, etc. — and even l'chatchila, etc. — something of its kind, etc., and so too in Sukkah, etc., for it would have seemed that since the remembrances are not upon it there is no name of shofar — for if they removed it and pierced it, it is invalid; if so, if they did not remove it and pierced it, it would have seemed that there is chatzitzah between the shofar. And it is — b'dieved it is not chatzitzah; nevertheless l'chatchila not. It teaches us that even l'chatchila we say: something of its kind is not interposing. And so said Rava in Sukkah daf 37b: it is permitted to insert the lulav within the binding of the hadas and aravah that were tied. And Lechem Chamudah: through the insertion its lulav leaves will fall and there will be chatzitzah. Something of its kind is not interposing. And so we rule siman 649 — behold that even l'chatchila we say something of its kind is not interposing:
magen-avraham/3:א: He intended to acquire. It implies in Tur and Beit Yosef and Rosh that even if it is of a non-Jew, if the Jew intended to acquire it, he did not fulfil — for it is idolatry of a Jew. And Bach wrote that it deals with idolatry of ownerless property; but if it has owners, even though he intended to acquire it he did not acquire it, and it is idolatry of a non-Jew, end quote. And it appears to us that we rule that a Jew does not annul idolatry of a non-Jew because of the decree lest he raise it for her and then annul it for her, and it becomes idolatry of a Jew, as is explained in Avodah Zarah 4, Mishna Berurah 12 — if so it is proven explicitly that even though it has owners it is called idolatry of a Jew. And so too in Tosafos Sukkah daf 31: if not, nothing would be difficult — for it should have said that it deals with idolatry that has an owner. And so too in Yevamos daf 104. And the reason: since the Jew is liable for it, it is called his; and so we find regarding chametz, and greater than this Bach wrote in Yoreh De'ah siman 146: some say that even if he did not acquire it, whenever his name is called upon it, it has no annulment. And even though we do not rule thus, and the proof he brings from "they participated" is not [valid], as explained in Kiddushin 17 — it is proven there that when they participated he acquired it before it came to his hand, see-there; nevertheless, when he acquired it, according to all it is forbidden even as theft:
magen-avraham/3:ב: When it was annulled from erev Yom Tov. But when it was annulled on Yom Tov — then it was rejected when Yom Tov entered, and again it is not seen, since he has no ability to fix it, for a Jew cannot annul it. But in a matter that he has ability to fix — even if it was seen and rejected, there was no deferral, as written siman 646 seif 2 (and in Beit Yosef): although it is forbidden to diminish them on Yom Tov, nevertheless it was in his power to diminish. And tzarich iyun in Yoreh De'ah siman 28 seif 1, that ruled like "the wind exempts" — even (if) it returned and was revealed (he is liable), for there is no deferral regarding a mitzvah; and it should have said that he should cover it (only) out of doubt, as written here — for in the gemara in Avodah Zarah daf 46 he compares them to each other. And so too Tosafos in Sukkah daf 33, see-there: this is called "not in his power," see-there on daf 32. And it appears that the view of Tur and Beit Yosef and the poskim is as Tosafos wrote in Avodah Zarah: the statement of Rabbi Levi is only l'chatchila; and with this all the difficulties that Tosafos challenged in Sukkah, see-there, are resolved. And if so the law is thus: b'dieved he fulfilled even without annulment, and l'chatchila he should not take it even after it was annulled, for it is repugnant before Heaven. And so too siman 154 seif 1. And according to this it must be that that which is written in siman 11 seif 8 "wool is invalid" — that is l'chatchila, for b'dieved he fulfilled; and the same applies that a horn is invalid l'chatchila for a shofar, and there it deals with idolatry of a Jew, except that through a non-Jew it is not forbidden, and nevertheless it is repugnant before Heaven:
magen-avraham/8:ב: And a measure of tekiah remained, etc. — tzarich iyun: why should this be worse than a hole, where even if a measure of tekiah did not remain it is kosher, as Bach wrote explicitly. And it is possible: since they tied it, it is as though they sealed somewhat. And tzarich iyun in Kol Bo:
magen-avraham/8:ו: And there are, etc. But in glue it is not of its kind, and its law is as written in seif 7:
mishnah-berurah/7:ה: (30) As it was initially — before it was pierced; and all the more so if its sound is similar only to the sound before the sealing:
mishnah-berurah/7:י: (35) There is [room] to permit, etc. — for we rely on the poskim who hold that wherever there are two [reasons] for leniency it suffices. And see in Peri Megadim who wrote that it appears one may bless, and especially according to what Peri Chadash and the Gra wrote, that the main [view] is like this opinion:
mishnah-berurah/8:י: (46) They glued with glue — and this is not called "not of its kind," for cracked is different from pierced, for the glue is not recognizable between the glue layers. And if the crack is wide and the glue is recognizable, certainly one should be strict about this, for it is as sealing with something not of its kind. And nevertheless it is possible that if its sound was not changed through the glue from what it was initially, one should not be strict when the majority remained, for also regarding a hole sealed in this manner it is kosher according to many poskim, as stated above in seif 7, and tzarich iyun:
mishnah-berurah/22:א: (87) Outside the techum — meaning even outside twelve mil, which is d'oraisa according to some poskim; and if so, according to them it is forbidden to tell a non-Jew to bring it, for they did not permit in the previous seif only something that is d'rabbanan. Nevertheless, if he brought it, even for the sake of a Jew, it is permitted to blow with it. And the reason: for behold something that comes from outside the techum is permitted in moving, and it is forbidden only in eating or benefit — namely to use it, as written in siman 495. And this that one blows with it a tekiah of a mitzvah is not considered benefit, as we wrote in siman 586. And nevertheless it is forbidden to move it in the city street whose entrances are not fixed in the form of a doorway outside four cubits, as explained in siman 495 [but if they are fixed through eruvin as required, it is considered like a house and permitted to move throughout]. A Jew who sent a shofar to another city through a non-Jew before Rosh Hashana, and the non-Jew was delayed and brought it on Rosh Hashana from outside the techum, and the people of the city did not know they would send them a shofar — one may not move it, and even blow with it if possible with another; and in a time of need there is [room] to permit. And the source of this law was explained at the end of siman 495 in the gloss, see-there, in Mishna Berurah:
peri-megadim/1:א: Of a ram. Taz, Magen Avraham 1: l'chatchila we require specifically bent; of a ram — only a preferred mitzvah. And if so, other species — bent and ram straight: if it happened so, or bent that he made more straight than the mitzvah requires — other species are required. And that which is written explicitly in Rabbeinu Moshe z"l in Beit Yosef in the name of Orach Chayyim: deer and ibex and wild goats are included in sheep. And nevertheless there are other species whose horns are hollow — a minority of animals' horns, and the like — and invalid according to Rabbeinu Moshe z"l, for there is no species of sheep at all; and according to Rosh and Tur it is kosher. And it is difficult how he wrote that Rabbeinu Moshe [agrees] like Rosh and Tur; also apparently "ram" in kamatz-yod is a species of wild animal — "ayalah ta'arog al afikei mayim, eil zachar" — "keves" with yod in chirik, and tzarich iyun greatly. And chapter "Re'eh" — and aku in Targum, and ya'ala as Rashi z"l explained: Steinbock; and Tosefta [Rosh Hashana] 27b s.v. shel ya'el — Rashi z"l explained: ya'el is an animal that walks in Bekaa; and in Rashi I did not find "chaya." And see Chullin, goats in Aleph-Lamed-Alef, see-there. And that which is written "keves" — apparently one could say that keves includes ewe and goat; and I would say that tzon includes ewe and goat, and likewise seh includes both; but keves implies only specifically the species of sheep, and tzarich iyun. And in any case chapter 1 halachah 1 of Shofar in the name of Kol Bo, see-there:
peri-megadim/3:_: And it is. Taz in Bach challenged Beit Yosef: if the shofar has owners, it is not that if a Jew acquired it — even if he intended to acquire it — it is nothing; rather it deals with [idolatry] of ownerless and stolen, in his view. But Taz explains according to its plain sense that the non-Jew did not intend that the Jew acquire it, only to steal it; but if a non-Jew gives him the shofar as a gift, then it is of a Jew, and its measurements [apply]. And Magen Avraham 5 explains [idolatry], and it will be explained there:
peri-megadim/10:_: There is [room] to permit. Taz: this is the view of the Rosh, that the Ran refers to [a case where] it hinders the tekiah, as written in letter 6. And here is view 1: its sound returned as it was before the hole; and the same if the sound did not change due to the hole and they sealed it of its kind — it is kosher if the sound is as it was. And per Rosh — even if its sound did not return to as much as it was before it was pierced, and all the more so if it returned to as much as it was before it was pierced. And it is possible: if it was pierced and its sound did not change, and when they sealed it of its kind its sound changed — the Rosh would concede it is invalid in such a case. And the view of Taz z"l: everything of its kind is not a shofar; and another matter from the language of the Rosh z"l — but of its kind, even if its sound changed, the reading is not "another matter causes the change of sound," etc.; it appears that even after the sealing the sound changed, and before the sealing the sound did not change — it is kosher when of its kind. The Rosh further challenged view 1: why when its sound did not return to what it was before it was pierced — only its sound as it was after it was pierced — why is it invalid according to view 1? And on this Beit Yosef and Taz explained according to its method; but per Rosh z"l, of its kind it is kosher in every matter, as stated above apparently:
rabbi-akiva-eiger/12:_: seif 12 in the gloss — the same law. And it is in Shulchan Aruch below siman 590 seif 9:
rabbi-akiva-eiger/7:_: Magen Avraham section 24. And he resolved that it deals outside twelve mil. It implies that also on Yom Tov outside twelve mil it is d'oraisa. And see responsa Bach HaChadashot siman 7 and in the last pamphlet there siman 36. And nevertheless I have a question: for from d'oraisa it is permitted by the law of within [the techum], like taking out a shofar to blow with it. And tzarich iyun. And in Sefer Tashbatz part 2 matter 213 it is explained that he holds that also on Yom Tov techum is d'oraisa. And it appears to me there is proof to infer thus from the words of the Rambam chapter 8 halachah 10 of Laws of Eruvin and in Maggid Mishneh: regarding techum there is no distinction between Yom Kippur and Yom Tov. And see in the gloss above siman 246 in Magen Avraham seif 12:
rabbi-akiva-eiger/8:_: Magen Avraham section 25. Tzarich iyun. See in responsa of the Rashba part 1 siman 22:
turei-zahav/7:ד: If the majority remained whole. And Tur wrote that if the majority of the shofar did not remain — even though a measure of shofar remained from the place of the hole until the placing of its mouth — it is forbidden, even though regarding cracked [shofar] for its width it helps; and the reason is that nevertheless here there is a shofar sound with another matter — namely the sealing:
yad-ephraim/8:_: And likewise the Rosh wrote explicitly, and thus: etc. I did not understand his proof from the Rosh — for there it deals when its voice changed after the sealing as well; but in truth also before the sealing there was a change of voice, and specifically regarding the factor of the emergence of the sound one may distinguish between of its kind and not of its kind. Again I saw in the Rosh that there is a textual error in Taz, and there it reads: no other matter causes the change of voice, etc. — meaning not of its kind: since there is sealing, also after opening we say that through the sealing the change was made, since no other matter causes the change of voice — we have no concern about it; and the words of Taz are correct:
